items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 4 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Keep meal times steady around your shifts
items.text: You work nights, so clock-time rules about late dinners don't fit you. Keep your main meal at the same point in your waking day.
